clue.text: One-off programme, possibly, featuring religious set

parts.note: PI is a familiar short form of pious, meaning religious
a lot is a set of items, as sold together at auction

explanation.surface: A one-off TV show built around a religious group of people.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a trial episode: a one-off programme that may or may not lead to a series.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial television episode, made to test whether a series will follow, is often a one-off programme.

clue.text: Choose a couple of items, without wife to criticise

parts.note: to pick is to choose

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letter for wife is dropped from the word for a couple

parts.note: a couple is two
pieces are items

explanation.surface: Selecting a few things while the wife is not there to disapprove.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick something to pieces is an idiom for to find fault with it in detail.

clue.text: Bright, topless bar

indicators.note: the top letter, in a down clue the first, is removed

parts.note: bright means clever

explanation.surface: A clever bar featuring topless dancers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless bar' suggests a club, but bar is the definition and 'topless' cuts the first letter from CLEVER.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigid bar used to prise or lift things is a lever, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Bird changes colour

parts.note: turns means changes, as leaves turn
a tone is a shade of colour

explanation.surface: A bird alters its colouring.
explanation.definitionFit: A small wading bird that flips over stones looking for food.

clue.text: Resolute policeman retained printout

indicators.note: one word holding another inside it, as something retained is kept within

parts.note: hardy means bold and resolute
cop is slang for a policeman

explanation.surface: A determined police officer held on to a printed document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resolute' tempts as HARD alone, but then the final Y has no source; resolute here is HARDY, which holds the policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: A printout on paper is a physical document, the computing term for which is a two-word phrase.

clue.text: Appetite is much larger about noon

indicators.note: one piece goes round another

parts.note: huger means much larger

explanation.surface: Hunger is much greater around midday.
explanation.definitionFit: A desire for food is an appetite.

clue.text: Prepares some pastry, bread being unavailable

parts.note: rolls are bread
out means not available

explanation.surface: Making pastry because the bread has run out.
explanation.definitionFit: A cook flattens pastry with a rolling pin, so preparing pastry is this phrasal verb.

clue.text: Dish and cup nearly match

indicators.note: the word is not quite complete, losing its final letter

parts.note: a tie is a match, as a cup tie

explanation.surface: A dish and a cup that almost match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dish' looks like crockery beside 'cup', but it is slang for an attractive person.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang an attractive person is a dish, as is a cute one.

clue.text: Empire-building socialist exposed for the first time?

indicators.note: the letters are built into a new structure

parts.note: red is a socialist

explanation.surface: An empire-building socialist is unmasked for the first time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empire-building' reads as one adjective for a power-hungry politician, but splits into fodder and anagram signal; the definition's question mark flags a socialist exposed as a show premiered.
explanation.definitionFit: A film or play shown for the first time has been given a first performance, laid open to the public.

clue.text: Explanatory note protecting landlord

parts.note: covering something protects it
a landlord is one who lets property, a letter

explanation.surface: A note of explanation that shields the owner of a rented house.
explanation.definitionFit: A short letter sent with a document to explain what it is and why it is enclosed.

clue.text: Kaleidoscope designer

parts.note: read as a person who designs kaleidoscopes, but it describes the toy itself, which makes coloured designs

explanation.definitionFit: A kaleidoscope creates ever-changing symmetrical designs, so it is a maker of patterns.

clue.text: They flog most of the bacon slices

indicators.note: the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: rashers are slices of bacon

explanation.surface: People who sell off most of the sliced bacon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flog' looks like 'sell', the British slang sense, but here it means beat: those who thrash. 'most of' trims THE to TH.
explanation.definitionFit: To flog someone is to thrash them, so people who flog are those who thrash.

clue.text: Priest's reportedly linked with a woman

indicators.note: the word is as heard, said rather than written

parts.note: Eli is the priest in the Old Testament who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: A priest is rumoured to be romantically involved with a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's given name, a short form of Elizabeth, so it can stand for a woman.

clue.text: Cannon ball

definitions.meaning: an automatic quick-firing anti-aircraft gun, named for its sound
a woolly ball used to decorate a hat

explanation.surface: A cannon fires a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a rapid-fire naval gun and a fluffy decorative tuft.

clue.text: Crooked importers falsify accounts

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dishonest importers cook the books.
explanation.definitionFit: To give a false account of events is to falsify accounts, in the sense of reports.

clue.text: Bus tour disrupted by Etna's second eruption

indicators.note: a disrupted tour is thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged
the second letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A coach trip is spoilt when Mount Etna erupts again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disrupted' rearranges BUS TOUR into OUTBURS, then 'second' takes T from Etna's. 'eruption' sits naturally with the volcano but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden outpouring, of anger or noise, is an eruption in the figurative sense.

clue.text: One making a song and dance, notice, always

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance
an ad is a notice
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, always

explanation.surface: A performer who makes a song and dance about things, all the time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a song and dance' looks like the fuss idiom, but the definition stops at song; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A singer of ballads is one who makes, or performs, a song.

clue.text: Matt put on top of gloss? That creates confusion

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: flat paint is matt, not shiny
spin is a gloss put on news, a favourable slant

explanation.surface: Applying matt paint over gloss makes a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: Matt and gloss look like paint finishes; gloss here is spin, a slant on facts.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a state of panic or agitation is an idiomatic sense, taken from an aircraft spinning horizontally out of control.

clue.text: See flower is protected in wind

indicators.note: one piece is shielded inside the other

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city and bishop's see in Cambridgeshire
the aster is a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: Look, a flower is sheltered from the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is not 'look' but a bishop's diocese; Ely, in eastern England, is the crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A wind blowing from the east is called by this name, used as a noun.

clue.text: Cover fitted in German plane

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: a lid is a cover

explanation.surface: A lid fitted to a German aeroplane.
explanation.definitionFit: An engineless aircraft that rides air currents is a kind of plane.

clue.text: Hungarian dog, namely, starts to snap like Alsatian

parts.note: viz is the abbreviation for videlicet, namely

indicators.note: the first letters of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: A Hungarian dog that snaps just like an Alsatian.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hungarian breed of gundog, sleek and russet-coloured, is a dog from Hungary.

clue.text: Leave former partner upset

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
to eat someone is to bother them, as in what's eating you

explanation.surface: Walking out on an upset ex.
explanation.walkthrough: An exeat is leave of absence, from a school or college, from the Latin for 'let them go out'.
explanation.definitionFit: A permission for temporary absence, granted at boarding schools and colleges, is a form of leave.

clue.text: Contender loses heart after start of the competition

indicators.note: one piece follows the other
the first letter of the word is taken
the middle letter is removed

parts.note: a rival is a contender

explanation.surface: A competitor loses heart once the contest begins.
explanation.definitionFit: A test of skill, as in a sheepdog contest or time trial, is a competition.

clue.text: Order restricting island's ethnic customs

indicators.note: one piece hems in the other

parts.note: trim means order or condition, as in in good trim
Bali is an Indonesian island; the possessive adds S

explanation.surface: A decree that limits the customs of an island's ethnic groups.
explanation.definitionFit: Loyalty to one's own tribe and its ways describes a set of ethnic customs or attitudes.

clue.text: Old Greek discovered Minoan piece, with odd bits missing

indicators.note: the letters in odd positions are dropped, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: An archaeologist finds a Minoan fragment with some parts missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered' is a link meaning found in.
explanation.definitionFit: An Ionic person belonged to the ancient Greek people of Ionia, so it can be an old Greek.

clue.text: Writer, torn apart, is bonkers

indicators.note: something torn is ripped up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A writer is so torn that he is going mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'torn' looks to belong with 'apart' as a phrase, but it is the signal and 'apart is bonkers' is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian author of Doctor Zhivago, a novelist and poet, is a writer.

clue.text: Olympic venue admits a legendary runner …

indicators.note: one piece lets another in

parts.note: Atlanta hosted the 1996 Olympic Games

explanation.surface: An Olympic host city welcomes a famous athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: The heroine of Greek myth was a swift runner who raced her suitors.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek huntress who raced her suitors and lost only to Hippomenes is a runner of legend.

clue.text: … one taking part in run after run?

definitions.text: one taking part in run after run?

indicators.note: one piece comes after the other

parts.note: a race is a run
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Somebody who enters one race after another.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue follows on from 25 across. 'after' puts R, for run, after RACE; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone competing in races is one taking part in runs, one after another.
